prompt:
Write a Node.js ES module semver.mjs in the current folder (no npm packages) that implements semantic version parsing and comparison. It must export these three functions by name.

parse(text) takes a string like "1.2.3", "v1.2.3", "1.2.3-alpha.1" or "1.2.3-rc.1+build.5" and returns a plain object { major, minor, patch, prerelease, build }. major, minor and patch are numbers. prerelease is an array of identifiers where identifiers made only of digits are converted to numbers and all others stay strings ("alpha.1" becomes ["alpha", 1]). build is an array of strings ("build.5" becomes ["build", "5"]). Both arrays are empty when the version has no such part. One leading lowercase "v" is accepted and ignored. Anything else that is not a valid version throws an Error whose message starts with "Invalid version". Invalid inputs include: non string values, an empty string, leading or trailing spaces, "1.2", "1.2.3.4", numbers with leading zeros such as "01.2.3" (but "0.2.3" is fine), an empty prerelease such as "1.2.3-", and a numeric prerelease identifier with a leading zero such as "1.2.3-01" (an identifier like "0a" or just "0" is fine).

compare(a, b) takes two version strings and returns -1 when a is lower than b, 0 when they are equal in precedence and 1 when a is higher. Compare major, then minor, then patch as numbers (so 1.10.0 is higher than 1.9.0). A version with a prerelease is lower than the same version without one. When both have prerelease parts, compare identifiers left to right: two numeric identifiers compare as numbers, a numeric identifier is lower than a text one, two text identifiers compare by plain string comparison (character code order, so "Beta" is lower than "alpha"), and if all shared identifiers are equal the version with fewer identifiers is lower. Build metadata is ignored, so "1.0.0+a" and "1.0.0+b" compare as 0. compare throws the same Invalid version error for bad input.

sortVersions(list) returns a NEW array with the same strings sorted from lowest to highest precedence using compare. The input array is not modified. Versions that compare as equal keep their original relative order.

For example the ordering 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-alpha.beta < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 < 1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0 must hold.
